question: Should OpenClaw ship this Discord subagent-progress mode with seven operator settings and the proposed shared channel lifecycle contract?
rationale: This is a new bundled user capability and public configuration/plugin-contract expansion, not a repair to an established behavior contract, so a maintainer must choose the permanent product and API surface.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded design
options.body: Keep the feature default off, fix the test and config blockers, require exact-head proof, and approve the shared lifecycle seam as the supported contract.

options.title: Reduce the public surface
options.body: Keep the visible Discord behavior but remove nonessential settings or shared adapter additions before re-review.

options.title: Do not ship in core
options.body: Close the proposal if maintainers do not want this Discord-specific progress mode as bundled product behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded design
recommendation.body: Keep the feature default off, fix the test and config blockers, require exact-head proof, and approve the shared lifecycle seam as the supported contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans both the existing Discord status-reaction presentation and the subagent lifecycle owner boundary affected by this decision.
